overview: Structure of Indian Society: 16 official questions – 2017 (3), 2019 Mains (2) and 2024 Prelims (11). 2024 concentrated on marriage (7): divorce forms, Kerala/ancient customs, Hindu Marriage Act sections, tribal marriage types. Religion and tribe get a few; family, caste, ethnicity and women have no official question yet, though other APPSC sociology papers ask them often.

possibility.angle: Concepts and methods – leadership, attitude scales
possibility.what_they_ask: Term for a definition (leadership), name of a measuring scale (Thurstone).

possibility.angle: Family – types, joint family, family laws
possibility.evidence: 0 official Qs; frequent in other APPSC sociology papers
possibility.what_they_ask: Natural targets: family of orientation vs procreation, matriarchal/patriarchal, Irawati Karve and K.M. Kapadia on the joint family, Nair tharavad, causes of joint-family decline.

possibility.angle: Marriage – forms, customs, divorce, HMA provisions, same-sex marriage
possibility.what_they_ask: Name of a custom (Niyoga, Sambandham), tribal marriage type (Diku Andi), form of talaq under challenge, HMA section number, first South Asian country to register same-sex marriage.
Identify the blood relation in a family puzzle.
Natural targets: Sanskritisation and dominant caste (M.N. Srinivas), Ghurye's features of caste, Dumont's Homo Hierarchicus, jajmani system, anuloma/pratiloma.
Festival → State, Census figure on ST households, chair of the 2013 tribal status committee.
Natural targets: ethnic group vs race vs tribe definitions, North-East ethnic identities, International Mother Language Day (21 Feb).

possibility.angle: Religion – rituals, sociological theories of religion
possibility.what_they_ask: Which community follows a ritual (Santhara, Dakhma), who gave a quoted theory of religion.

possibility.evidence: 0 official Qs; related APPSC exams ask quotes and laws
possibility.what_they_ask: Natural targets: author of a quote on women's status (K.M. Panikkar), women-related Acts (Dowry 1961, Domestic Violence 2005), matrilineal communities (Khasi, Nair).

traps.trap: Gives a ritual of a neighbouring religion [community swap]
traps.spot: Options mix Jain, Parsi, Buddhist and Sufi terms
traps.fix: Santhara/Sallekhana and Aparigraha = Jain; Dakhma (Tower of Silence), Shenshai = Parsi.

traps.trap: Swaps the tribe for a marriage type
traps.spot: Each option pairs a marriage form with a tribe
traps.fix: Diku Andi = marriage by negotiation (Ho); probation = Kuki; capture = Naga.
traps.pyq: Diku Andi → negotiation in Ho tribes [prelims-2024#63]

traps.fix: S.5 conditions: (iv) prohibited degrees, (v) sapinda; S.12 voidable; S.13 divorce.

traps.trap: Gives the struck-down talaq instead of the one now challenged
traps.fix: Talaq-e-biddat (instant) struck in 2017; Talaq-e-Hasan (three monthly pronouncements) challenged later.

traps.spot: Kinship puzzle with spouses and in-laws as options
traps.fix: Consanguineal = by blood (uncle–niece); spouses and in-laws are affinal.

traps.trap: Gives a neighbouring theorist of religion
traps.spot: Quote on religion with Durkheim, Malinowski, Parsons
traps.fix: Death/anxiety and emotional stress as source → Malinowski; sacred–profane, collective conscience → Durkheim.
Hornbill – Nagaland; Sangai – Manipur; Chapchar Kut – Mizoram; Wangala – Meghalaya.

techniques.name: Community-term sorting [religion tags]
techniques.how: Tag each option term with its religion; the answer is the one tied to the stem's community.
techniques.example: Zoroastrian excarnation: Aparigraha and Sallekhana are Jain, Shenshai is a Parsi calendar sect → Dakhma [prelims-2024#62]

techniques.name: Blood-line tracing
techniques.how: Draw the family tree; join only by parent–child links. Any link that passes through a marriage is affinal.
techniques.example: Krishna → parents → sister Madhavi → daughter Jyothi: only blood links → Krishna and Jyothi [prelims-2024#66]

techniques.name: Region/period anchor for customs
techniques.how: Place the custom by region and era: Kerala matriliny, ancient Hindu law, tribal India.
techniques.example: Nair–Namboothiri matrilineal union → Sambandham [prelims-2024#85]; ancient procreation custom → Niyoga [prelims-2024#88]

techniques.name: Committee-by-year
techniques.how: Tie tribal committees to years: Dhebar 1960-61, Bhuria 2002-04, Xaxa 2013-14.

techniques.name: Current-law check
techniques.how: For 'first/recent' legal questions, recall the latest status in each country or court.
techniques.example: Nepal registered a same-sex marriage in 2023; India's SC did not recognise it → Nepal [prelims-2024#120]

confusions.remember: Jain fast unto death vs Parsi Tower of Silence.
Blood relation vs relation through marriage.
Instant triple talaq (struck 2017) vs three pronouncements over three months.
Single pronouncement + iddat vs delegated right of divorce to the wife.
Levirate-type procreation custom vs hypergamy / hypogamy.
Nair–Namboothiri union vs matrilineal joint household.
Religion from anxiety and death vs from the sacred and collective life.
Equal-appearing intervals vs agree–disagree / social distance.
Ability to influence vs legitimate power.
Born into vs created by marriage.

anchors: Santhara / Sallekhana – Jain ritual fast unto death.
Diku Andi – marriage by negotiation among the Ho.
HMA 1955 – S.5(v) sapinda bar; S.12 voidable; S.13 divorce.
Talaq-e-biddat struck down in 2017 (Shayara Bano); criminalised by 2019 Act.
Xaxa Committee – set up 2013 on tribal socio-economic, health and education status.
Nepal – first South Asian nation to register a same-sex marriage (2023).
Malinowski – death and anxiety as sources of religion.
Irawati Karve – joint family as an extended kinship group; K.M. Kapadia – 'Marriage and Family in India'.
checklist: Which community or tribe does the stem name? Tag each option to its community.
For kinship, draw the tree and check for any marriage link.
Law questions: recall the exact section and the latest court status.
Theorist quotes: match the key idea (death, sacred, function) to the thinker.
For an angle not yet asked (caste, family, women), expect definitions and author–concept pairs.
